steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: PAPC: Platform Mediation for Privacy-Propagation Externalities in AI-Mediated Workflows
summary: It replaces final-output-only privacy filtering with interception of information-moving events (memory writes, inter-agent messages, tool calls, workspace updates) before they reach shared state, deciding among allow, abstract, quarantine, block, or rights-narrowing. The cost is an additional policy, provenance, and content-analysis layer on every event, adding latency and engineering complexity to the orchestration stack, plus ongoing policy authoring and maintenance. It can fail through misconfigured policies that either leak raw values via missed event paths or over-quarantine and break task completion, and its guarantees depend on the platform controlling all shared-state channels, which third-party API-based agents may not permit.
rationale: The approach addresses a real failure mode in multi-agent systems, but adopting it requires control over the event plane and workload-specific policy tuning that the reader must validate before production reliance.
technique: Event-level privacy mediation for agent workflows

claims.statement: It replaces final-output-only privacy filtering with interception of information-moving events (memory writes, inter-agent messages, tool calls, workspace updates) before they reach shared state, deciding among allow, abstract, quarantine, block, or rights-narrowing. The cost is an additional policy, provenance, and content-analysis layer on every event, adding latency and engineering complexity to the orchestration stack, plus ongoing policy authoring and maintenance. It can fail through misconfigured policies that either leak raw values via missed event paths or over-quarantine and break task completion, and its guarantees depend on the platform controlling all shared-state channels, which third-party API-based agents may not permit.

PAPC reportedly preserves deterministic task completion and eliminates measured exact raw-value and external raw-value exposure on retrieval-memory and multi-agent benchmarks; no quantified factor is given.
